h1: The 7 Best Mini Printers for Small Spaces of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Mini Printers, Small Spaces: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven compact printers for small spaces, from inkless thermal models to Canon, HP and Epson all-in-ones, with tradeoffs.
summary: The Epson EcoTank ET-2800 is the best mini printer for frequent printers thanks to its refillable tanks, flatbed scanner and wireless printing. The Canon TR160 is the battery powered portable pick. Canon's TS4320 and TR4720 and the HP DeskJet 4355 cover the cartridge based middle, while two inkless thermal models suit tiny spaces.
intro: Small printers hide their costs. The compact body that fits your shelf can quietly drain money in cartridges, while the inkless thermal model that tucks into a drawer cannot print color at all. Size is only one of four trade-offs, and it is rarely the one that bites later.

Seven compact printers made this ranking, from tank based inkjets to pocketable thermal units. Our editors scored them from listed specifications: ink system, scan and copy features, duplex support, connectivity and portability. Nothing here is based on print quality claims, since the sources give none.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2800 Wireless Color All-in-One Cartridge-Free Ink Supertank Printer
products.verdict: Refillable ink tanks, scanning and wireless printing for frequent printers.
products.description:
The Epson ET-2800 is a color all-in-one with refillable ink tanks instead of cartridges, plus a flatbed scanner and copier and wireless printing. It ships with startup ink bottles and sits in the $100 to $200 tier.

It wins because tanks go straight at the cost that hurts compact inkjets most: refills. The Canon TS4320 sits in a similar footprint class, but it runs on cartridges and comes in cheaper upfront, which is the whole trade. The Canon TR160 is more portable but has no scanner.

Buy it if you print color regularly from a small office or desk. Skip it if you print rarely, or if you need the smallest body possible, since the tank design makes it larger than the thermal and battery models.
products.idealFor: Small home offices that print color often.
products.skipIf: You print rarely and need the smallest body.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR160 Wireless Portable Lightweight Compact Printer with Battery
products.verdict: A rechargeable battery lets it print away from an outlet.
products.description:
The Canon TR160 is a portable wireless inkjet with a rechargeable battery, a 1.44 inch display and a 50 sheet paper tray. It lives in the $100 to $200 tier, the same as the Epson above it.

It takes second place because it is the only inkjet in the list that can print away from an outlet. The ET-2800 beats it on features because it offers a scanner and copier, which the TR160 lacks, and tanks over cartridges for running costs.

It suits people who print at home and sometimes on the road, at a hobby stall or in a rented room. The honest caveat is that it cannot scan or copy, so anyone who handles paperwork should look at the Canon TS4320 or Epson instead.
products.idealFor: People who print at home and on trips.
products.skipIf: You need to scan or copy.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS4320 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer for Duplex Printing
products.verdict: A small color inkjet with duplex printing and a scanner.
products.description:
The Canon TS4320 is the most compact true color inkjet here: duplex printing, a flatbed scanner and copier, wireless connectivity and easy setup, in the $50 to $100 tier. Duplex support lets it print on both sides of a page automatically.

It ranks third because it uses regular cartridges, which means ongoing cost over time, unlike the Epson. It beats the HP DeskJet 4355 on the duplex feature that the HP does not list, and it undercuts the Epson on price.

Choose it for a small desk that needs color, duplex and a scanner without the larger tank body. The caveat is cartridge spending and no document feeder, so multi page scans mean lifting the lid for each sheet.
products.idealFor: Small desks needing color and duplex.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer, Scanner, Copier
products.verdict: Compact all-in-one with scan and copy and the HP Smart app.
products.description:
The HP DeskJet 4355 is a compact color all-in-one with scan and copy functions, wireless printing and HP Smart app support. It includes a 3 month Instant Ink trial and falls in the $50 to $100 tier.

It ranks fourth because the listing shows no duplex printing, which the Canon TS4320 offers, though the HP adds app control that makes setup and phone printing simpler. Against the TR4720, the HP is a lighter feature set without a document feeder or fax.

It suits small spaces that want basic all in one use and prefer an app driven setup. The honest caveat is that the Instant Ink trial is temporary, so factor in what you will actually pay for ink once the trial ends.
products.idealFor: Small spaces needing basic all-in-one use.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer with Auto Document Feeder
products.verdict: An auto document feeder for multi-page scanning in a compact body.
products.description:
The Canon TR4720 is a compact wireless all-in-one with an auto document feeder and built in fax, listed in the $50 to $100 tier. The feeder is the headline: you can scan or copy a stack without lifting the lid for every page.

It sits fifth because the feeder adds bulk compared with the TS4320, and it uses cartridge ink. It is also the only printer in this ranking with fax, which will matter to a few buyers and no one else.

Buy it if you occasionally scan multi page documents, contracts or forms, and still need to keep the footprint small. Skip it if the smallest body is the priority. The caveat is that it feels larger than the TS4320, and the extra mechanism is wasted if you rarely scan.
products.idealFor: Multi-page scanning in a compact space.

products.name: Gloryang Inkless Portable Printer, Wireless Thermal Printer with Carry Case
products.verdict: Inkless thermal printing with a carry case and three paper rolls.
products.description:
The Gloryang is an inkless Bluetooth thermal printer that supports 8.5 by 11 inch thermal paper. It ships with a carry case and three paper rolls, and is listed in the $50 to $100 tier. There is no ink to buy or spill.

It ranks sixth because thermal printing is monochrome and needs special paper, which the inkjets above avoid. It beats the NDYIN on the bundled case and rolls, though it costs more.

It suits drawer storage and light printing, such as forms, shipping labels or school work in a tight space. The caveat is ongoing paper cost and the lack of scanning. If you ever need color or copies, one of the Canon or Epson all-in-ones is a better home.

products.name: NDYIN Portable Printer Wireless, N80 Bluetooth Inkless Thermal Printer
products.verdict: The smallest option, with no ink cartridges to store.
products.description:
The NDYIN N80 is an inkless Bluetooth thermal printer supporting Letter and A4 thermal paper, with iOS, Android and laptop compatibility. It carries the lowest price tier in the ranking, at $25 to $50.

It ranks last because it ships without the Gloryang's carry case and bundled rolls, even though it is the cheaper of the two. It also shares the thermal limits: monochrome output, special paper and no scanning.

Buy it if you have almost no space, print occasionally from a phone and do not want ink cartridges around. Skip it if you want color or a scanner. The honest caveat is that thermal paper has to be restocked, so check what the paper costs before you commit.

whatMatters.detail: The ink system is how the printer stores and delivers ink. Cartridges are cheap upfront but expensive over time, tanks refill from bottles, and thermal printers need special paper instead. It matters because running costs outweigh purchase price for frequent users. Look for cartridge free or inkless wording in the listing title.

Scan and copy means a built in flatbed that lets one device replace a separate scanner. It matters for forms, receipts and IDs in a small workspace. Check the title for scan and copy, and look for an automatic document feeder like the Canon TR4720 if you scan multi page stacks.

Duplex printing is automatic two sided output. It saves paper and cuts the number of pages you handle. Among these printers, the Canon TS4320 lists it in the title. If you print long documents, look for the word duplex in the listing, since many compact models skip it.

Connectivity is how the printer receives jobs. Wireless suits a shared network, while Bluetooth suits a phone for the thermal models. It matters because setup and sharing depend on it. Confirm the listed connection type and whether an app such as HP Smart is required.

Portability is whether the printer can work away from a wall outlet. A rechargeable battery, as on the Canon TR160, makes travel printing possible. Look for battery power in the specs, and check the paper tray size, since the TR160's 50 sheet tray sets the practical print run.

faq.a: No. The NDYIN N80 and Gloryang are inkless and use thermal paper instead. That saves cartridges but means you must keep stocking compatible paper, and output is monochrome.

faq.q: What mistake do buyers make with mini printers?
faq.a: Ignoring ongoing ink cost. A cheap cartridge printer such as the Canon TS4320 can cost more over a year than the tank based Epson ET-2800 if you print a lot. Compare ink or paper costs.

faq.q: Is the EcoTank worth it over the Canon TS4320?
faq.a: If you print often, the tanks target lower running costs, which is where compact inkjets hurt. If you print rarely, the Canon TS4320 costs less upfront and ink in the cartridges will not dry out as long.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Use the maker's app or the printer display to join your Wi-Fi network, or pair over Bluetooth for the thermal models. The HP DeskJet 4355 works through HP Smart, and the Canon TR160 has a small display for setup.

Keep the printer covered and use only the paper types in the listed specs. Thermal models such as the Gloryang need thermal paper, and tank printers like the Epson should be printed regularly to keep ink flowing.

faq.q: Can I print from a phone?
faq.a: Yes for the models that list it. The NDYIN N80 lists iOS and Android support, the Gloryang uses Bluetooth, and the HP DeskJet 4355 prints through the HP Smart app. Check the other listings for app details.

finalTake: If you print often, the Epson ET-2800 is the one to buy, because its tanks attack running costs. The Canon TR160 is the travel friendly choice, and the TS4320 is the budget color all-in-one. Choose a thermal model only if drawer storage matters more than color, and always compare ink or paper costs before the sticker price.
